params.body:
Follow-up to #42. `hand.mjs policy sign` on the laptop first reads the draft from Portal, and that read needs a Portal token too. On 8 October it stopped with "No way to Portal: no token" before anything was signed.

`policyDraft()` now reads the draft through the box when this machine holds no token and is not a hand that signs its own reads. That is the laptop's case. It goes the way the laptop already reaches the gateway: over ssh with the owner's key, running curl on the box with Elixir's Portal token (`/home/elixir/elixir-secrets/portal-token`). The draft route admits fabric. The token is read on the box and never leaves it.

The workbench (token-less, but a hand that signs its reads) and any machine with a token keep the Portal route.

**Not tested end to end:** from the workbench the box offers only the door, not a shell, so the token path follows Elixir's config (`elixir.portal_token_file` in the secrets directory) and is not observed. If it differs, the error names what the box answered.
